One of these two tasks will be performed next. Option 1: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop.
Option 2: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling a copy of itself. To prevent an endless loop, the function must include a "base case" that stops the self-calling when a specific condition is met. Imagine a set of Russian nesting dolls, where opening each doll reveals a smaller one inside until you finally reach the smallest, solid doll that cannot be opened. By breaking a large problem down into these progressively smaller, identical steps, recursion allows computers to solve complex tasks elegantly.
